title: Cochrane-Style Systematic-Review Methodology for the AI Safety Index

original_idea.body:
# Cochrane-Style Systematic-Review Methodology for the AI Safety Index

**Problem:** The FLI AI Safety Index scores labs, but its methodology is a single-pass expert judgment. Evidence-based medicine developed rigorous systematic-review protocols (inclusion criteria, evidence grading, inter-rater reliability) that the Index doesn't use.

**Direction:** Transfer Cochrane/GRADE systematic-review machinery. Re-score one Safety Index dimension for several labs using an explicit inclusion-criteria + evidence-grading protocol, compute inter-rater reliability against the published scores using two independent coders (or two LLM passes), and report where the rigorous protocol disagrees with the Index.

**Why it matters:** Strengthens a widely-cited governance benchmark with reproducible evidence-grading, advancing international consensus on evaluation methodology. Builds directly on the strategy hint to extend the AI Safety Index methodology.

**Relevant context:** FLI AI Safety Index (public methodology + scores); GRADE/Cochrane systematic-review standards; strategy hint FR67 (apply AI Safety Index methodology to additional dimensions).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: rigorous re-scoring strengthens a cited governance benchmark, but catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Re-score one Index dimension with GRADE protocol plus inter-rater reliability; intermediate desk work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a re-scored dimension with IRR; few dependencies.

novelty.reasoning: Extends FLI Safety Index (existing) with systematic-review machinery; partly open methodological add-on.
